title: EFC — Master Specification
description: Formal master specification of Energy-Flow Cosmology (EFC), defining the dynamical energy-flow field, an effective potential coupled to entropy, an entropy-modulated expansion rate, and an entropy-dependent effective light speed. The paper unifies rotation curves, lensing behavior, and late-time acceleration as emergent thermodynamic effects without invoking non-baryonic dark matter or an external dark-energy component.

energy_flow_alignment.description: To leading order, the scalar energy-flow field aligns with the negative entropy gradient, organizing energy transport along entropy-driven channels.

effective_potential_linear.description: Baseline effective potential coupling the energy-flow field to the entropy level; A_{\Phi} sets the potential amplitude.

effective_potential_general.description: General non-linear family where \beta modulates the strength of coupling between energy flow and entropy.

expansion_rate.description: Effective expansion rate derived from the magnitude of the energy flow modulated by entropy; enables late-time acceleration without an external dark-energy term.

rotation_curves.description: Effective circular velocity from the radial gradient of the effective potential, producing thermodynamic rotation curves without dark matter.

entropy_midpoint.description: Defines the low-entropy (s0) and high-entropy (s1) endpoints and their midpoint and span.

normalized_entropy_coordinate.description: Normalized entropy coordinate used in the effective light-speed law.

variable_light_speed.description: Entropy-dependent effective speed of light with a minimum at the mid-entropy level; modulates focusing/defocusing and light-travel times.

light_travel_time.description: Observed photon travel time along path \gamma through regions with varying effective light speed c(S).

key_results.main_finding: Defines a thermodynamically coupled dynamical-structural-light propagation framework where rotation curves, lensing profiles, and cosmic acceleration emerge from the fields (E_f, S) and c(S) without dark matter or external dark energy.

sealed_predictions.statement: Mid-entropy regions (near S_mid) produce systematically longer light-travel times (time-delay plateaus) along lines of sight crossing those regions due to the minimum of c(S).
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Strong-lens time-delay measurements and FRB/pulsar timing through mapped entropy proxies showing no correlation between delays and mid-entropy structures.

sealed_predictions.statement: Galactic rotation-curve plateaus arise without non-baryonic dark matter, stabilized by the entropy-driven c(S) minimum near S_mid and the potential \Phi(E_f,S)=A_\Phi E_f(1+S).
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: High-resolution rotation curves with spatially resolved entropy proxies (e.g., thermodynamic/entropy maps) failing to predict plateau amplitude and radius from the specified \Phi and c(S).

sealed_predictions.statement: Lensing exhibits a dual-profile: low-entropy regions act as focusing wells while high-entropy regions contribute to large-scale defocusing.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Weak/strong lensing maps cross-correlated with entropy/structure indicators that do not show the predicted focusing–defocusing asymmetry.

sealed_predictions.statement: Late-time acceleration can be reproduced from evolving (E_f,S) via H(E_f,S)=\sqrt{|E_f|(1+S)} without an external dark-energy component.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Distance–redshift and growth-rate measurements requiring an additional dark-energy term beyond the H(E_f,S) form.

kill_criteria: KC1: Precise time-delay measurements (e.g., lensed quasars, FRBs, pulsars) through well-mapped mid-entropy regions show no increase in delays relative to comparable paths, contradicting c(S)=c0(1+a_edge x^2) with a minimum at S_mid.
KC2: Systematic failure to reproduce galaxy rotation-curve plateaus and shapes using \Phi(E_f,S)=A_\Phi E_f(1+S) and entropy/flow maps, while standard dark-matter profiles succeed on the same sample.
KC3: Lensing convergence and shear maps show no correlation with entropy proxies expected for the dual focusing (low S) and defocusing (high S) behavior predicted by EFC.
KC4: Cosmological distance–redshift data and structure growth jointly require an external dark-energy component incompatible with H(E_f,S)=\sqrt{|E_f|(1+S)} across redshifts.
KC5: Independent constraints demand an effectively constant speed of light along astrophysical lines of sight at levels that rule out any observable entropy-dependent modulation of c(S) as specified.
KC6: Direct laboratory/astrophysical probes of entropy gradients fail to align with the predicted energy-flow alignment E_f \propto -\nabla S in regimes where EFC applies.
